title: Runtime attention kernel exchange probe and canary plan
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Safely integrate and validate FlashAttention v2 and v3 variants into the runtime kernel selector while preventing regressions for prefill and decode scheduling. We observed non-deterministic P95 regressions and occasional OOMs for short-prefill/long-decode patterns after landing a v3-weighted kernel scoring change in staging. This ticket coordinates profiling, microbenchmarks, heuristic improvements, and a metricized canary rollout (and rollback) to ensure safe deployment to production.
context_and_background: Recent kernel selector changes expanded candidate list to include multiple FlashAttention variants. On staging we saw: (1) increased prefill latency for batch shapes with many short sequences, (2) transient workspace estimation mismatches that triggered slower fallback paths, and (3) higher variance in decode steady-state under interleaved prefill+decode workloads. Root cause hypotheses include workspace overprovisioning in v3's allocator, microbatching interaction with the scheduling queue, and kernel startup jitter when switching kernels mid-epoch.
outcome_and_objectives: 1) Determine safe selector heuristics that prefer v3 when it improves throughput without increasing P95 or OOMs. 2) Add runtime safeguards and a deterministic prober to detect shape-specific regressions. 3) Implement a canary rollout with automated metrics gating and clear rollback triggers. 4) Deliver monitoring dashboards and a postmortem template for any observed regressions.
acceptance_criteria: P95 token latency for representative workloads does not increase by >5% compared to baseline (runtime-1.19) across canary nodes
No increase in OOM rate (events per 100k requests) on canary nodes versus baseline
Canary monitors (latency, token/sec, errors) and rollback automation in place before widening rollout
PRs for kernel-selector heuristic and prefill scheduler changes merged and CI green
Benchmark suite (prefill microbench + mixed prefill/decode scenarios) added to perf-harness and reproducible locally
plan: Phase 0: Baseline collection - run existing perf suite across representative models (chat, code, embeddings) and record kernel profiles (workspace, startup cost, steady throughput)
Phase 1: Deterministic prober - add a synthetic prober that exercises short-prefill/long-decode and varied batch shapes to reproduce observed jitter

Phase 2: Heuristic updates - change kernel-scorer to include workspace-safety margin and a startup_latency_penalty for candidate kernels; add memory-aware route that prefers stable-layout kernels under tight workspace budgets
Phase 3: Staging validation - run prober and real-traffic shadowing on dedicated staging nodes with v2 and v3 enabled, collect 48h metrics
Phase 4: Canary - 1% traffic for 24h, automated gating on latency P95, error rate, token/sec. If stable, widen to 10%, then 50% and full rollout
Phase 5: Post-rollout - run extended spot-checks and schedule follow-up tuning for any persistent anomalies
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: v3 workspace estimator underestimates causing OOMs - Mitigation: conservative safety margin and fallback to v2/legacy kernels when workspace check fails
Risk: microbatching interplay increases latency variance - Mitigation: introduce microbatch hysteresis and prefer steady-state layout for prefill-heavy requests
Risk: Canary false positives due to noisy tenant traffic - Mitigation: use controlled synthetic prober and compare to shadow baseline alongside production canary metrics
implementation_notes:
- Added detailed instrumentation hooks: kernel_choice, workspace_req, actual_workspace, startup_ms.
- Updated kernel-scorer to compute a safety_score = workspace_margin*2 + startup_penalty*1.5 + tail_latency_penalty.
- Prefill scheduler: prefer contiguous prefill ordering for KV-cache-friendly model families; apply interleaving only when decode latency budget allows.
- New perf harness: mixed_prefill_decode_v2 (shapes derived from 7 live customers).
artifacts_and_links: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/11845 - prober harness and synthetic workloads
Incidents reference: INC-2025-0012 (OOM observed during v3 experiment)
comments: 2025-01-13 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial profiling run completed for 5 model families. v3 shows 8-12% throughput win for long-prefill large-seq workloads but 6-9% P95 regression for short-prefill shapes on A100 nodes.

2025-01-16 - Marco Ruiz: Reproduced workspace mismatch locally. v3 allocator reports lower required workspace but kernel path ends up allocating more due to alignment behavior. Opened PR #11823 with conservative workspace margin implementation.
2025-01-22 - SRE (Lin Chen): Staging quota request approved. Reserved 4 canary nodes with mixed GPU families for experiments. Added node tags runtime-canary-v3.

2025-01-28 - Marco Ruiz: Ran 48h staging run. Observed transient OOMs at 03:12 UTC (2 events) on node runtime-canary-v3-02. OOMs tied to bursty prefill patterns when microbatcher combined many tiny sequences. Patching microbatcher hysteresis in PR #11845.
2025-02-02 - Aisha Kapoor: Canary 1% scheduled for 2025-02-03 08:00 UTC. Gating thresholds: P95 delta >5% OR OOM events >0 triggers immediate rollback. Monitoring alerts preconfigured.
2025-02-03 - Marco Ruiz: Canary started. Initial 2h snapshot: P95 delta +1.2% (within threshold), token/sec +3%. No OOMs. Continuing 24h validation.
